title: China completes world's third robotic arm-assisted heart transplant
key_facts: Surgeons at the First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University in Xi'an, Shaanxi province, carried out a heart transplant using robotic arms on 5 Oct 2026, China Daily reports.
The patient was a 67-year-old man with end-stage heart failure and several other illnesses, for whom a traditional operation that splits the breastbone was judged too risky.
The surgeons made one incision of about 8 centimeters between the ribs plus two small ports for the robotic arms, without breaking the breastbone.
Deputy director Li Yongxin controlled the robotic arms with his thumbs and index fingers and implanted the donor heart.
The article calls it the first such operation in China and the third in the world; Saudi Arabia did the first in 2024 and the United States in 2025.
The donor heart resumed beating; the patient came off the ventilator the same day, and the surgeons say he now walks daily and his heart function has fully recovered.
Surgeon Yan Yang, director of cardiovascular surgery at the hospital, says robotic transplantation is still at an early, exploratory stage and may eventually become routine, including remote surgery.
quote_evidence: The surgery is the first of its kind completed in China and the third in the world, and it offers a new and safer surgical option for patients with end-stage heart failure.
Using robots in heart transplantation remains in the early exploratory stage.
Saudi Arabia did the first surgery in 2024 for a 16-year-old patient, and the United States did it in 2025 for a patient in their 40s.
why_it_matters_hint: A less invasive way to transplant a heart could help high-risk patients, but this is one reported case described by the hospital's own surgeons.
event_date: Surgery on 5 Oct 2026; China Daily report dated 16 Oct 2026
notes: Single outlet (China Daily, state-run) and one patient; recovery claims are the surgeons' own. The surgery was on 5 Oct 2026 but the only public report found is dated 16 Oct 2026, so it looks like a first announcement; marked FOLLOW-UP of 5 Oct 2026 because the underlying event is earlier, and the main session can decide if it counts as old news. The robotic arms are controlled by a surgeon, not autonomous.
